# Whole-app review — StockInvoice (v2.6.0)

**Scope:** 9,484 lines of Python across 82 modules, 6,760 lines of Jinja across 67 templates, plus CSS/JS, config, migrations and tests. **Nothing was modified** — this was read-only, plus a local smoke run I've since shut down (`git status` still shows only your two pre-existing edits to [main.css](app/static/css/main.css) and [run.py](run.py)).

**What I ran:** `python -c "from app import app"` (clean, 127 routes), the dev server with read-only `curl` probes, a live MongoDB inspection of collections/roles/indexes, a cookie-header inspection through Flask-JWT-Extended, `pytest --collect-only`, and static analysis of route guards, templates and translations.

---

## Critical

**1. Unauthenticated super-admin password reset backdoor**
[app/blueprints/web/auth/routes.py:20](app/blueprints/web/auth/routes.py#L20) and the identical block in [app/blueprints/mobile/auth/routes.py:25](app/blueprints/mobile/auth/routes.py#L25): any anonymous POST to `/web/auth/login` carrying `reset_admin_password=1` and `email=admin@si.ma` sets that account's password to the hardcoded `admin123`. No session, no token, no rate limit. The README instructs creating the super admin at exactly `admin@SI.ma`, so this targets the documented super-admin account — and [CHANGELOG.md:22](CHANGELOG.md#L22) advertises it as a feature. It is a one-request account takeover of the highest-privileged user.

**2. Secrets are the published placeholder values**
`.env` has `SECRET_KEY` and `JWT_SECRET_KEY` matching the literals in `.env.example`, which is committed to the repo. Anyone who can read the repository can forge session cookies and JWTs for any identity. PyJWT also emits `InsecureKeyLengthWarning` at token creation — the JWT key is 31 bytes, below the 32-byte HS256 minimum in RFC 7518 §3.2.

**3. RBAC is never enforced**
`has_permission()` and `UserModel.has_perm()` have **zero call sites** outside their own definitions. `ALL_PERMISSIONS`, `expand_permission`, `get_effective_permissions` — the entire [permissions.py](app/core/utils/permissions.py) module is decorative. The only real checks are two role-name string tests (`super_admin_required`, `_company_admin_required`). [PROJECT_SUMMARY.md](PROJECT_SUMMARY.md) claims "route-level 403 enforcement"; its own "Suggested Next Steps" says to add it. Authorization is currently `@jwt_required()` plus ad-hoc `company_id` string comparisons.

**4. The `roles` table is empty, so `/admin` is unreachable for everyone**
Live DB: `roles: 0`, and both users have `roles: ['Customer']` with `company_id: None`. `super_admin_required` needs `'Admin'` in the JWT `role_names` claim, so every existing user — including `admin@stc.ma` — gets 403 on the admin panel, and `UserModel.to_dict` computes `permissions: []` for all of them. [migrations/migrate_to_rbac.py](migrations/migrate_to_rbac.py) seeds roles but was never run here; [fixes/fix_roles.py](fixes/fix_roles.py) is a hand-patched workaround for the same gap. The migration is a manual, undocumented step.

**5. Cross-tenant reads for users without a company**
- **EShop public catalog:** [eshop/routes.py:29](app/blueprints/eshop/routes.py#L29) builds `filters = {'status': 'active'}` with **no `company_id`** when unauthenticated → anonymous visitors get every tenant's active products. `/eshop/item/<id>` likewise resolves any tenant's product.
- **Invoice/stock create:** [invoices/routes.py:56](app/blueprints/web/invoices/routes.py#L56) falls back to `ProductModel.find_all_unpaginated()` with an empty filter when the JWT has no `company_id` → all tenants' products.

This isn't hypothetical: both live users have `company_id: None`, so they hit that branch today. (With 0 products in this database the pages render empty, which is why it hasn't been noticed.)

---

## High

**6. No CSRF protection.** `JWT_COOKIE_CSRF_PROTECT = False` in [config.py:16](app/config.py#L16), no Flask-WTF, no token in any of the ~100 forms. I dumped the actual auth cookie: `access_token_cookie=…; HttpOnly; Path=/` — **no `SameSite`, no `Secure`**. Protection rests entirely on browsers' default Lax behavior, and `GET /web/auth/logout` is state-changing, which Lax still sends. `[app/config.py:16](app/config.py#L16)` also hardcodes `JWT_COOKIE_SECURE = False`.

**7. Error pages leak internals.** [error_handlers.py](app/core/utils/error_handlers.py) renders `error_context(e)` — script filename, function name, line number and raw exception text — into the 500 HTML *and* the JSON body.

**8. `/eshop/admin` is dead code that fails open on the wrong axis.** [eshop/routes.py:84](app/blueprints/eshop/routes.py#L84): `if role_names not in ("Admin", "Manager")` compares a **list** against a tuple of strings, so it's always true → `abort(403)`; but that `abort` sits inside `try/except Exception`, which swallows it and redirects to the dashboard. The page never renders for anyone, and the 403 never surfaces. The correct check is commented out on the line above.

**9. No rate limiting anywhere** — no limiter, lockout, backoff or throttle on login or registration.

**10. Open self-registration with no company binding.** `/web/auth/register` is public and `AuthService.register` assigns `roles: ['Customer']` with no `company_id` — a self-service path straight into finding #5.

---

## Medium

**11. No indexes.** Only `_id_` exists, on `users` and `events`; every other collection has none. Login (`find_by_email`), all company-scoped list queries and every `count_documents` are full collection scans — and there is no unique index on `users.email`, so uniqueness rests on an application-level pre-check.

**12. Admin dashboard N+1.** [admin/routes.py:54](app/blueprints/admin/routes.py#L54) runs 7 `count_documents` per company, then 10 global counts and two aggregations, on every page load.

**13. Per-render DB work.** The `inject_globals` context processor does two lookups on **every** template render including error pages ([app/__init__.py](app/__init__.py)); `UserModel.to_dict()` issues a roles query each call and is invoked repeatedly per request.

**14. ~430 lines of dead parallel layer.** `app/models/`, `app/services/`, `app/utils/`, `app/extensions.py` are imported only by `app/blueprints/auth/`, `invoice/` and `stock/` — none of which are registered in the app factory. Two competing `AuthService`, `InvoiceService`, `StockService` and `UserModel` exist.

**15. PDF generation depends on the working directory.** [pdf_service.py:38](app/core/services/pdf_service.py#L38) opens `app/static/fonts/…` and `app/static/uploads/logos/{logo}` as relative paths — run the app from any other directory and every invoice PDF fails.

**16. Debug mode is the documented default.** `run.py` sets `debug=True` when `FLASK_ENV=development`, which both `.env.example` and your live `.env` use — the Werkzeug debugger and its PIN are exposed. `gunicorn==26.0.0` is pinned but there is no Procfile, gunicorn config, or documented start command anywhere.

**17. Git hygiene.** `app/static/uploads/` is gitignored, yet 5 logos totalling 6.2 MB are already tracked — ignore rules don't apply to tracked files, so those binaries are in history permanently while new uploads silently won't be. `run.py` also picked up a stray UTF-8 BOM from your uncommitted edit.

**18. The test suite does not run.** `pytest --collect-only` fails with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'playwright.sync'` and **aborts collection** (3 tests collected, 0 executed). No `conftest.py`, no pytest config, no CI. `tests/` is really ad-hoc DB scripts (`test_connection*.py`, `migrate_*.py`, `debug_login.py`) mixed with Playwright browser tests, and both `pytest` and `playwright` sit in production `requirements.txt` next to `gunicorn`.

---

## Low / quality

- **i18n gap:** 508 distinct `_('…')` keys in templates, 469 have AR/FR entries → **131 (26%) fall back to English** (`About Us`, `Access Denied`, `Action`, `Accent Color`…). Some are placeholders like `'+123 456 7890'`, so the real gap is smaller but material.
- **CDN without SRI:** Bootstrap, bootstrap-icons and Chart.js from jsdelivr plus Google Fonts, no integrity hashes. [orders/printable.html:6](app/templates/orders/printable.html#L6) pins Bootstrap **5.3.0** while [base/layout.html:79](app/templates/base/layout.html#L79) pins **5.3.3**.
- **Packaging:** 11 blueprint subpackages have no `__init__.py` (they work only as implicit namespace packages); `app/blueprints/web/services/` holds nothing but `__pycache__` and `app/templates/services/` is empty — yet README lists **Services** as "Ready".
- **Doc drift:** README claims mobile routes use "different templates" (they render the same web templates) and lists a `/web/services/` route that doesn't exist; `PORT` default is documented as 5002 while your local `run.py` binds `127.0.0.1`.
- **Error handling style:** 80 `except Exception`, 2 bare `except:`, 5 that `pass`, 47 `print()` calls alongside a proper logging setup. `abort(403)`/`abort(404)` inside `try` blocks get silently converted to flashes and redirects (see #8).
- **Missing hardening:** no CSP / `X-Frame-Options` / HSTS / `X-Content-Type-Options`; `CORS(app)` with library defaults; `set_lang` redirects to unvalidated `request.referrer` (open redirect); invoice numbers `I{ddmmyy}-{count+1}` are derived from a count and collide after deletions.

---

## What's genuinely good

The app factory imports cleanly with 127 routes and no import-time surprises. Layering into models/services/validators is sensible, and **tenant scoping is consistently threaded through the invoice, order and stock services** — `get_by_id(id, cid)` compares against the JWT claim, never client input, and I verified that pattern holds across the module. All ~100 business routes carry `@jwt_required()`, and an anonymous browser request correctly 302s to login (confirmed live; API clients get 401). bcrypt hashing, an 8-char/letter/digit password policy and real email validation are in place. Jinja autoescaping is left on and the only `|safe` uses are `|tojson|safe`, which is correct — no XSS sink in templates, and no `innerHTML` with user data in shipped JS. Request logging carries method, path, duration, user and IP, with login/logout audit events.

## Critical

**1. Unauthenticated super-admin password reset backdoor**
[app/blueprints/web/auth/routes.py:20](app/blueprints/web/auth/routes.py#L20) and the identical block in [app/blueprints/mobile/auth/routes.py:25](app/blueprints/mobile/auth/routes.py#L25): any anonymous POST to `/web/auth/login` carrying `reset_admin_password=1` and `email=admin@si.ma` sets that account's password to the hardcoded `admin123`. No session, no token, no rate limit. The README instructs creating the super admin at exactly `admin@SI.ma`, so this targets the documented super-admin account — and [CHANGELOG.md:22](CHANGELOG.md#L22) advertises it as a feature. It is a one-request account takeover of the highest-privileged user.

**2. Secrets are the published placeholder values**
`.env` has `SECRET_KEY` and `JWT_SECRET_KEY` matching the literals in `.env.example`, which is committed to the repo. Anyone who can read the repository can forge session cookies and JWTs for any identity. PyJWT also emits `InsecureKeyLengthWarning` at token creation — the JWT key is 31 bytes, below the 32-byte HS256 minimum in RFC 7518 §3.2.

**3. RBAC is never enforced**
`has_permission()` and `UserModel.has_perm()` have **zero call sites** outside their own definitions. `ALL_PERMISSIONS`, `expand_permission`, `get_effective_permissions` — the entire [permissions.py](app/core/utils/permissions.py) module is decorative. The only real checks are two role-name string tests (`super_admin_required`, `_company_admin_required`). [PROJECT_SUMMARY.md](PROJECT_SUMMARY.md) claims "route-level 403 enforcement"; its own "Suggested Next Steps" says to add it. Authorization is currently `@jwt_required()` plus ad-hoc `company_id` string comparisons.

**4. The `roles` table is empty, so `/admin` is unreachable for everyone**
Live DB: `roles: 0`, and both users have `roles: ['Customer']` with `company_id: None`. `super_admin_required` needs `'Admin'` in the JWT `role_names` claim, so every existing user — including `admin@stc.ma` — gets 403 on the admin panel, and `UserModel.to_dict` computes `permissions: []` for all of them. [migrations/migrate_to_rbac.py](migrations/migrate_to_rbac.py) seeds roles but was never run here; [fixes/fix_roles.py](fixes/fix_roles.py) is a hand-patched workaround for the same gap. The migration is a manual, undocumented step.

## What this final session changed

Picking up from the interrupted run, three things remained:

1. **A real CSRF bug the verification caught.** Flask-JWT-Extended only honours the `X-CSRF-TOKEN` header unless `JWT_CSRF_CHECK_FORM` is enabled — it was off, so the hidden `csrf_token` field that [main.js](app/static/js/main.js) injects into every server-rendered form was silently ignored. Every classic HTML form POST (create invoice, save settings, …) would have 403'd. Set to `True` in [config.py](app/config.py).
2. **Misleading 403 page.** [error.html](app/templates/base/error.html) hardcoded "Access Denied" for all 403s and discarded the handler's message, so an expired form token looked like a permissions problem. The 403 branch now renders the actual message (CSRF → "Your form token is missing or expired…").
3. **Re-verification** — the earlier session's mobile-auth read turned out to be stale; the backdoor removal, login throttling and registration gate were already on disk there too.

**Critical**
- **Password-reset backdoor removed** from both [web/auth/routes.py](app/blueprints/web/auth/routes.py) and [mobile/auth/routes.py](app/blueprints/mobile/auth/routes.py) — anonymous POSTs with `reset_admin_password=1` no longer set `admin123`; the template field is gone.
- **Placeholder secrets rejected.** [config.py](app/config.py) refuses example/short keys via `validate_secrets()` (hard failure in production, warning in dev); `.env.example` now documents generating strong values. Live config reports `insecure_secrets: []` and no `InsecureKeyLengthWarning`.
- **RBAC enforced centrally.** A `before_request` gate in [app/\_\_init\_\_.py](app/__init__.py) resolves each endpoint to a permission via [route_permissions.py](app/core/utils/route_permissions.py) and checks `UserModel.has_perm()`. [bootstrap.py](app/core/utils/bootstrap.py) seeds the 3 roles and 24 MongoDB indexes idempotently at startup and via `flask bootstrap` — the live DB now has `Admin/Manager/Customer` instead of 0 roles.
- **Cross-tenant leaks closed.** Company-less authenticated users are refused all tenant-scoped blueprints (redirected to their dashboard), and service-layer lookups (`StockService`, `InvoiceService`, orders, events) now filter by `company_id`; verified by a cross-tenant invoice read returning redirect.

- **CSRF active** (double-submit cookie + form/header injection, `SameSite=Lax`, `COOKIE_SECURE` env flag) with a proper 403 handler.

- **Registration gated** behind `ALLOW_PUBLIC_REGISTRATION` (default off), both surfaces.
